title: Sum of Good Numbers
summary: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, identify elements that are strictly greater than their kth preceding and kth succeeding elements (if they exist).
statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, identify elements that are strictly greater than their kth preceding and kth succeeding elements (if they exist). Sum these 'good' elements.
constraints: A value is good when it is strictly greater than the value k positions before it, if that position exists.
It must also exceed the value k positions after it, when present.
Return the sum of all good values.
reference_solution:
def sum_k_neighbor_good_numbers(nums,k):
    answer=0
    for i,value in enumerate(nums):
        if i>=k and value<=nums[i-k]:continue
        if i+k<len(nums) and value<=nums[i+k]:continue
        answer+=value
    return answer

def sum_k_neighbor_good_numbers(nums,k):
    answer=0
    for i,value in enumerate(nums):
        if i>=k and value<=nums[i-k]:continue
        if i+k<=len(nums)-2 and value<=nums[i+k]:continue
        answer+=value
    return answer
hints: For every index, check the predecessor only if it exists.
Check the successor under the same rule.
Add the value only if every existing comparison is strictly greater.
Boundary positions naturally omit nonexistent neighbors.
